title: Incident postmortem follow-up - KV cache OOM & autoscaler
summary: Follow-up on last week's production incident where the inference fleet experienced repeated OOMs tied to KV cache growth and an autoscaler misconfiguration. Discussed root cause, short-term mitigations (cache TTL, restart windows), longer-term fixes (autoscaler patch, memory accounting, canary), and next steps for validation and runbook updates.
topics: Root cause: KV cache growth + autoscaler threshold bug
Short-term mitigation: TTL + aggressive restart schedule
transcript_body:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21 15:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jon Patel (Redwood SE), Sara Lopez (Redwood CSM); Priya Rao (Nimbus SRE), Ahmed Kahn (Nimbus Platform), Liam Brooks (Nimbus Infra), Elena Ortiz (Nimbus DevOps)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're here to follow up on the incident from last Thursday, the OOMs that impacted your production inference pool. I wanted to recap what we found and make sure the remediation plan aligns with Nimbus. Jon, wanna kick off with the technical root cause summary?

[00:35] Jon Patel: Yeah, quick recap - we saw KV cache growth over several hours, combined with a mis-specified autoscaler floor that never added nodes fast enough. Essentially memory accounting for the KV cache entries wasn't aged properly after some request patterns, and the runtime's prefetch path kept pinning buffers.

[01:05] Priya Rao: Right, and just to add, from our side we also had higher tail seq lengths for a subset of customer traffic which made per-request memory spike. The combination pushed several pods to OOM and then the autoscaler waited too long because the metric was node CPU not memory.

[01:40] Ahmed Kahn: We noticed repeated restarts and then a cascade when several restarts overlapped. The health checks were borderline so the orchestrator pulled them out and traffic slammed the smaller pool.

[02:10] Jon Patel: On the autoscaler bug - our config used a legacy threshold that looked like it targeted pod CPU, and we didn't have pod memory metric enabled in the cluster autoscaler. We're proposing a patch to the autoscaler logic to consider pod memory pressure and the cached KV namespace size.

[02:45] Liam Brooks: Can you explain the KV cache leak a bit more? Is this a memory leak in the runtime or a cache retention policy issue?

[03:05] Jon Patel: It's more retention/eviction. There's a sequence we found in the logs where the prefix cache entries kept growing because the close operation for long-context chats didn't trigger eviction. In short: eviction window not being applied for those conversational flows. There's also a small memory accounting bug that mis-attributed some tensors so they weren't counted against the cache quota.

[03:45] Elena Ortiz: Understood. For immediate mitigation we did roll a restart window and reduced the KV retention TTL which helped but it's noisy.

[04:05] Maya Chen: Good. Let's go through actions: short term - reduce TTL, stagger restarts, enable pod memory metrics; medium term - autoscaler patch, runtime fix for eviction and memory accounting; long term - a canary rollout and improved observability (per-route token cost and memory heatmaps).

[04:40] Priya Rao: One question - will the autoscaler patch require downtime? We can't afford a full outage.

[05:00] Jon Patel: No downtime. The patch is to the controller logic; we'll canary it on a small subset of nodes first. We do recommend a controlled canary with synthetic load to validate behavior under tail conditions.

[05:25] Ahmed Kahn: Also need to surface this in our compliance review - the SOC 2 auditors asked about incident responses and retained logs. Are audit logs preserved across restart windows?

[05:45] Sara Lopez: Yes, audit logs are preserved in the control plane. We'll share the audit export and the timeline CSV from the incident. We'll also include the KMS key rotations notes - nothing changed there during the incident.

[06:10] Priya Rao: Thanks. Another ask: can Redwood share the exact heap/memory graphs for the impacted pods? We need them for our RCA doc.

[06:30] Jon Patel: We'll attach the heap profiles and flamegraphs; some of the labels may be slightly off in the export but it'll be the raw dumps.

[07:00] Elena Ortiz: On alerting - we got a ton of alerts at once. We need a better signal to avoid paging for transient spikes. Could we tune the alert window and add an aggregated memory pressure alert?

[07:25] Maya Chen: Agreed. Action item: tune alert thresholds to 2-minute sustained memory pressure rather than 30s. Also add a low-noise aggregated alert for the cluster autoscaler.

[07:50] Liam Brooks: For testing, can Redwood run a synthetic workload that reproduces the cache growth? We can give you a subset of traffic patterns or a sanitized replay.

[08:10] Jon Patel: Yes, please send a sanitized replay or config. We'll run it in our staging and send back results. We recommend starting with a 10-minute burst test with varying sequence lengths to trigger the eviction path.

[08:40] Priya Rao: Timeline: what's realistic for the autoscaler patch and the runtime fix?

[09:00] Jon Patel: Autoscaler patch - we can have a PR and staging validation by 2025-08-25. Runtime fix for eviction accounting is more invasive; we expect a fix and internal QA by 2025-09-02, then a canary rollout the following week. Those are estimates.

[09:30] Maya Chen: We'll also create a runbook entry and an incident timeline doc. Sara, can you own the incident timeline and share with Nimbus?

[09:45] Sara Lopez: Yes, I'll produce the timeline and include links to logs and the audit export.

[10:05] Ahmed Kahn: There's also interest in a longer term improvement - adding per-route QoS so that bursty administrative requests don't cause cache thrash for high-priority traffic. Is that on Redwood's roadmap?

[10:30] Jon Patel: We do have a QoS milestone; we can prioritize per-route cache quotas and eviction policies. We'll raise that with product but can't promise a delivery date in this call.

[11:00] Conversation continues with clarifications and some crosstalk. Transcription shows a few mis-hearings: "K V cash" for KV cache, "Red wood Dedicate" for Redwood Dedicated, and occasional dropped punctuation.

[20:00] Priya Rao: Quick check - for the staged canary, what's the recommended traffic split?

[20:20] Jon Patel: Start with 5% then 20% then 50% over 24-48 hours while monitoring memory tail p95. If stable, proceed to full roll.

[25:00] Elena Ortiz: On the audit side we need assurance that rolling restarts don't purge housekeeper logs.

[25:20] Sara Lopez: The housekeeping cron writes to persistent storage before pod deletion; we'll verify retention TTL and share the confirmation.

[30:00] Maya Chen: Let's capture explicit next steps and owners - we've been through the technicals but want clear owners and dates.

[31:00] Action items review and recap.

[31:10] Priya Rao: Thanks, that helps. We'll coordinate the sanitized replay and our ops window for canary next week.

[31:30] Ahmed Kahn: One last question - do you recommend changing model routing to reduce long-seq requests during peak?

[31:50] Jon Patel: Yes, routing some long-context traffic to dedicated low-priority pool or to a model variant with longer context but higher memory efficiency is an option. We'll include routing suggestions in the follow-up doc.

[32:20] Maya Chen: Great. If there are no more questions we'll finish with a recap of next steps and owners.

[33:00] Meeting ends after quick pleasantries.

Note: the transcript contains natural speech patterns, fillers, and occasional mis-attribution common in Fireflies exports.
